Manufacturing location (historical): Previously manufactured at Elan factory in Austria [13] 16. Manufacturing energy: Made with 100% solar energy (per merchant) [1] 17. Nitro Slash model first year: The Slash has appeared in Nitro's line since at least 2011 (earliest user review found) [14]; The Good Ride has images dating back to 2011 and 2012 [15] 18. Major redesign year: 2021 — described as "a giant change from previous years, pretty much a completely new board" [16] 19. Camber change for 2023 (model year 2024/25): Changed from Cam-Out Camber to Trüe Camber; also gained 3D Surf Tech shaping [17] 20. Predecessor model camber (2024 model year and earlier): Cam-Out Camber — "a classic camber shape with early and smooth transitions into tip and tail" [18] 21. Current model camber: Trüe Camber — standard traditional camber for "stability, and pop" [19] 22. Shape: Tapered Directional — tail narrower than nose [1][20] 23. Camber type: Trüe Camber (True Camber) — strong snap and powerful response [1][19] 24. Core profile: Reflex Core Profile — thinner core between feet for improved handling and increased torsional flex [1][21] 25. Width designation: Wide [1][22] 26. Sidecut type: Progressive Sidecut — larger radius in nose blending into tighter radius in tail [1][23] 27. 3D shape: 3D Surf Tech — convex nose transitioning into front binding, concave tail for control [1][24] 28. Flex rating: 7/10 (mid-stiff) [1][25] 29. Flex pattern: Directional All Terrain Flex [26] 30. Mounting system: 2x4 Inserts [1] 31. Setback: -2.5cm (all sizes) [1] 32. Core: PowerCore II — tip-to-tail Poplar wood with additional Beech Wood stringers [1][27] 33. Laminate: Bi-Lite Laminates — fibres in two directions for strength, power, and forgiving feel [1][28] 34. Sidewalls: ABS Sidewall — flexible and impact resistant [1][29] 35. Base: Sintered EcoSpeed HD Base — sustainable, hard, durable, fast, high wax absorption [1][30] 36. Edges: Recycled Steel Edge [1][29] 37. Factory wax: Green Speed Natural Wax — 100% biodegradable, made from renewable resources [1][31] 38. Powder performance: Rated "Good" — very easy float, not the most setback surfy ride but "very competent" [58] 102. Base glide: Rated "Good" — decent but not amazing; can lose wax faster than some boards [58] 103. Carving: Rated "Great" — really back-foot-weighted turns, very satisfying spring out of turns [58] 104. Speed: Rated "Great" — some floppiness in nose at speed [58] 105. Uneven snow: Rated "Good" — a little bucky/bouncy in soft uneven snow, width can be fatiguing for smaller boots [58] 106. Switch riding: Rated "Average" — directional shape limits switch capability [58] 107. Jumps: Rated "Good" — great pop for a board with no carbon stringers [58] 108. Jibbing: Rated "Average" [58] 109. Pipe: Rated "Good" [58] 110. On-snow feel: Semi-locked in [58] 111. Turn initiation: Medium/Fast [58] 112. Skidded turns: Semi-Hard [58] 113. Buttering: Moderate [58] 114. Edge hold: Rated for "Hard Snow" — pretty good, nothing amazing [58] 115. Approximate weight feel: Normal — not heavy or light [59] 116. Positive: Very competent powder float [58] 117. Positive: Easy to access the poppy flex [58] 118. Positive: Very smooth, flowy, easy back-footed feel on groomers [60] 119. Positive: Eco-minded build praised — recycled edges, bio-based resins, Green Speed wax [50] 120. Positive: Great balance between being flexy/rubbery but still lively and poppy [58] 121. Positive: The 3D nose gives ultimate surfy feel in powder [61] 122. Negative: Only suited for back-foot-weighted turners — can be problematic for some riders [62] 123. Negative: Width can be fatiguing for steering from the front foot in uneven snow for smaller boot sizes (e.g. size 9 US) [63] 124. Negative: Base can get base-burn and lose wax faster than some boards [58] 125. Negative: 3D spoon nose can cause nose to wash out when buttering [58] 126. Negative: Not recommended for beginners — Nitro conservative with recommended weight [64] 127. Negative: Board graphics are size-dependent and cannot be changed between sizes [52] 128. Flex personality: Medium overall — medium stiff tail, medium flex between the feet, medium soft nose [58] 129. Flex category label (evo): Stiff (evo rates 6-8/10 as "Stiff" on their standardized scale) [65] 130. Flex category label (Tactics): Medium Stiff — "increased support and control for bigger or aggressive riders" [35] 131. 3D Surf Tech nose: Convex shape transitioning into front binding for ultimate surfy feel [24] 132. 3D Surf Tech tail: Concave shape for quick control and carve-ability [24] 133. 3D Surf Tech analog: "like a thruster fin setup" for surfiest feel all over the mountain [66] 134. Forum opinion: "Slash is one of those boards you're just gonna like regardless" [74] 148. Snowboard Robot review (2021): "much more stable than I expected from the length" and "The camber keeps it solid and poppy" [75] 149. User comment (Snowboard Robot): Slash is "a good short and wide option, without having to go for something as full on as the Fintwin or the Pow" [75] 150. The Good Ride sizing advice: Boot size is most important factor, weight second, height third [64] 151. The Good Ride recommended boot sizes 156cm: US 9-11 [58] 152. Angrysnowboarder: Nitro Slash listed as a contender for Top 5 Powder Boards of 2026 [76] 153. Volume-shifted concept: Board designed to ride one step shorter than standard length while maintaining surface area [38] 154. DISAGREEMENT — Camber type (2024 model): Some retailers list 2024 Slash as "Cam-Out Camber" [18] while others list it as "True Camber" with 3D Surf Tech [77].
